action_summary: Close the gap Wave 40's bench measured, using the refusal as the specification (K3=0, $0 spend): the Meaning-IR ratchet could apply a learned rule only verbatim inside the context it was learned in, so a target line with fresh identifiers, no `return`, or the comparison written the other way round declined with REFUSED__CROSS_LANGUAGE_TRANSFER_NOT_PRODUCED and nothing was done with the name. New canonical/swe_kernel/refusal_acquire_retry_v1.py reads that refusal as a specification: OperatorRewrite.from_tokens derives the rule's meaning (exactly one operator token changed, hole identities preserved, anything else refused by name); two application procedures are tried cheapest-first (DIRECT_OPERATOR_REWRITE, then INVERTED_OPERAND_REWRITE for the same predicate with its operands exchanged); a candidate is admitted only if the caller's verifier accepts it AND the target parses; the retry is reported with the verifier's word; and the procedure is remembered so the next refusal of the same kind costs one step instead of two. The ratchet now returns PASS__ACQUIRED_AFTER_REFUSAL with a refusal_acquisition receipt, or keeps its refusal status. The frontier bench gains a seventh measured class (REFUSAL_ACQUISITION_RETRY) whose refusal control catches a claim of success on an instance that can only be refused.
